title: Harry Potter
author: J.K. Rowling
short_summary: Harry Potter, an orphan kept in a cupboard under the stairs by the Dursleys, discovers on his eleventh birthday that he is a wizard and has a place at Hogwarts School of Witchcraft and Wizardry. There he makes his first real friends, Ron Weasley and Hermione Granger, learns why every witch and wizard knows his name — and works out that something hidden in the school is being hunted by the wizard who killed his parents.
extended_summary:
Harry lives in a cupboard under the stairs until letters begin arriving addressed to him there, and Hagrid finally delivers one in person. At Diagon Alley he buys a wand at Ollivanders — holly and phoenix feather — and is told that the wand chooses the wizard. On the Hogwarts Express he meets Ron Weasley; at the Sorting he is placed in Gryffindor, though the Hat considers Slytherin; and he makes an enemy of Draco Malfoy and, apparently, of Professor Snape.

A three-headed dog on the forbidden third floor, a Gringotts vault emptied the same day it was visited, and a name on a Chocolate Frog card — Nicolas Flamel — slowly assemble into one question: what is hidden at Hogwarts, and who wants it? Harry, Ron and Hermione work it out and go down through the trapdoor after it.

Underneath are the protections the teachers have built: Hagrid's three-headed dog, lulled by music; Professor Sprout's Devil's Snare; Professor Flitwick's flying keys; Professor McGonagall's giant chess set, which Ron wins by sacrificing himself; and Snape's row of seven bottles, which is not magic at all but a logic puzzle, and which Hermione solves. At the end Harry finds the Mirror of Erised, and Professor Quirrell — with Voldemort's face on the back of his head beneath the turban — cannot take the Stone from it, because Dumbledore's enchantment gives it only to someone who wants to find it and not to use it.

questions.prompt: Of all the protections guarding the Stone, Snape's is the odd one out. What kind of challenge is it?

options: A logic puzzle, with no magic involved at all
A duel against an enchanted suit of armour
A riddle that must be answered in Latin
A maze that rearranges itself as you walk

questions.explanation: Hermione says it out loud: this isn't magic, it's logic, and a lot of great wizards haven't got an ounce of it. Snape's trap is designed to stop a wizard rather than a thief — which is exactly why the one person who can pass it is the girl who reads.

questions.prompt: Snape's puzzle is a row of seven bottles. How many of them hold poison?

options: Three
Only one
Five
Six

questions.explanation: Three are poison, two are nettle wine, one takes the drinker forward through the black flames and one takes them back. Only one small bottleful of the forward potion is left, which is why Harry has to go on alone.

questions.prompt: In Diagon Alley, Mr Ollivander explains that you do not really pick your wand: it is the wand that chooses the ___.
questions.explanation: Harry's is holly with a phoenix-feather core — and Ollivander remembers that the same phoenix gave just one other feather, which went into the wand that gave Harry his scar. It is the first hint in the book that Harry and Voldemort are connected.

questions.prompt: Where do Harry, Ron and Hermione first come across the name Nicolas Flamel?

options: On a Chocolate Frog card of Dumbledore
In the restricted section of the library
On a label inside Harry's new cauldron
In a letter that Hagrid leaves behind

questions.explanation: Harry had read it on the train months earlier and remembers it at exactly the right moment. The name sits in plain sight for half the book on a collectable card — Rowling hides her clue where a child would actually look.

questions.prompt: Put the obstacles under the trapdoor in the order Harry and his friends meet them.

items: A three-headed dog that must be sent to sleep
A plant that grips tighter the more you struggle
A cloud of flying keys and a broomstick
A giant chess set that must be played to win
A row of seven bottles and a written riddle
A mirror that shows the heart's desire

questions.explanation: Each teacher contributed one protection, and each one needs a different kind of person to pass it. That is the design of the whole sequence: Harry could not have got to the bottom alone, and the book makes sure the reader notices.

questions.prompt: Match each teacher to the protection they set for the Stone.
questions.explanation: Every protection is in the style of the person who made it — Hagrid brings a monster and loves it, Sprout grows something, Flitwick makes things fly, McGonagall builds a game with rules. Working out who set what is half the fun of the chapter.

questions.prompt: Sort each obstacle by who actually gets the three of them past it.

options.label: The plant that squeezes tighter as you fight it
The seven bottles and the written riddle
Remembering what the Herbology lessons said
Catching the right key in mid-air on a broom
Standing in front of the Mirror of Erised
Facing the man under the turban alone

questions.explanation: Ron wins the chess game by sacrificing himself, Hermione gets them through two obstacles with reading and reasoning, and only the last three are Harry's. The famous 'chosen one' spends most of this chapter being helped.

questions.prompt: Quirrell stands in front of the Mirror of Erised and cannot get the Stone out of it, but Harry can. Why?

options: Only someone who wants to find it, not use it, can
Only a Gryffindor is able to open the mirror
Only a person under an invisibility cloak can
Only the youngest person in the room can take it

questions.explanation: Dumbledore built the last protection out of a character test rather than a spell. Quirrell wants to use the Stone and therefore only sees himself using it; Harry wants to stop him and has no use of his own for it, so it drops into his pocket.

questions.prompt: At the final feast Dumbledore awards points that change the result, including ten to Neville for standing up to his own friends. Was it fair to decide the House Cup like that, at the last moment, for things that happened in secret? Give your reasons.
questions.explanation: Both sides can earn full marks. A strong 'unfair' answer notices that Slytherin had already won on the year's work, that the points were awarded for rule-breaking, and that nobody else could have earned points that way. A strong 'fair' answer notices what the three actually did, and that Dumbledore deliberately includes Neville, whose act nobody would otherwise have seen. Accept either, argued from the book.

questions.prompt: Each teacher guarded the Stone with a challenge in their own style. Invent one more protection for the sequence: which subject would it come from, what would the challenge be, and what kind of person would get past it?
questions.explanation: There is no single right answer. A strong answer keeps the book's rule: the obstacle must match a real Hogwarts subject and must be passable by a particular *kind* of person — brave, clever, calm, good on a broom. An obstacle nobody could pass, or one that is simply 'very hard', misses how the chapter is built.

questions.prompt: The writing around the top of the Mirror of Erised is back to front. Read properly, it says: "I show not your face but your heart's ___."
questions.explanation: Dumbledore warns Harry that men have wasted away in front of it, not knowing whether what it shows is real or even possible. It is also why the Mirror makes such a good final guard: it traps anyone who wants the Stone for himself.

questions.prompt: What is hidden under Professor Quirrell's turban?

options: Voldemort's face, on the back of his head
A scar exactly like the one Harry has
The Philosopher's Stone, sewn into the cloth
A pouch of powdered unicorn horn

questions.explanation: Quirrell has been sharing his body all year, which is why he stammers, why he smells of garlic and why the classroom smells strange. The teacher everyone suspected — Snape — had in fact been trying to protect Harry the whole time.
